stories.headline: Death toll rises after powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake hits Colombia
stories.body:
A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia at 07:34 local time (12:34 GMT) on Monday [c2]. Rescuers searched under rubble across the region following what has been called the country's strongest earthquake this century [c1]. Official figures confirm that more than 180 people died in the earthquake, while aggregated figures from local officials indicate the death toll may exceed 240 [c3]. Meanwhile, the Colombian Association of Capital Cities reported that at least 132 people were killed and more than 570 were injured as of Monday afternoon [c16].

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella, who took office on the Friday preceding the earthquake [c18], declared a state of disaster and announced temporary rental subsidies for affected families [c14]. The president reported that almost 2,600 people were injured, nearly 200 remain missing, over 1,100 homes were destroyed, and over 8,000 homes were damaged [c4]. However, local authorities in western Colombia reported that more than 3,000 people remain missing and nearly 5,000 homes were damaged [c12]. In international developments, Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares reported that 164 Spanish citizens were missing in Colombia following the earthquake [c11]. To assist local rescue teams, the European Union activated its Copernicus satellite service to help Colombian authorities assess damage and carry out rescue operations [c15].

Major cities across western Colombia suffered heavy casualties and destruction. In Cali, Mayor Alejandro Eder reported 95 deaths, 239 people trapped, 949 injured, and 45 buildings partially or fully collapsed [c5]. In the city's Calima neighbourhood, four children died and 30 were referred to care centres after a section of the Gimnasio Calima school collapsed [c6]. To prevent looting, Mayor Eder ordered a curfew starting at 20:00 local time on Tuesday until 06:00 on Wednesday [c7].

In Pereira, 79 people were confirmed dead by the city's fire department, leading local authorities to implement a car-free day to facilitate search efforts [c9]. In Manizales, Mayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas stated that five people were killed and 60 buildings partially or totally collapsed in the city [c10]. Air travel in the region was severely disrupted, as airports in Quibdo, Pereira, Manizales, Armenia, Cartago, and Buenaventura were closed due to earthquake damage [c13].

The earthquake was followed by significant seismic activity. Colombia's geological service reported that more than 70 aftershocks occurred following Monday's earthquake, including two 3.6-magnitude quakes early on Tuesday [c8]. This disaster comes after recent regional tragedy, as twin earthquakes struck the northern coast of Venezuela on June 24, killing more than 6,000 people [c17].

vocab.meaning: An order requiring people to stay indoors during specified hours.
Smaller earthquakes that follow a larger earthquake in the same area.

stories.headline: Syrian court sentences ousted president Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia
stories.body:
A court in Syria has sentenced ousted President Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher al-Assad to death in absentia for crimes committed during the country's 14-year civil war, which claimed approximately 500,000 lives [c27]. The Damascus court also sentenced four other former military and security officials to death in absentia, including former defense minister Fahd al-Freij [c23]. Bashar al-Assad had become the designated heir to the presidency after his older brother, Basil, died in a car accident in 1994 [c29]. He fled Damascus for Moscow with his family after his regime was overthrown in December 2024 [c20]. Ahmed al-Sharaa subsequently became president of Syria following an 11-day campaign that ended the Assad family's rule [c24].

Syrians gathered outside the Justice Palace in Damascus following the rulings [c19]. Former political security head in Daraa province, Atef Najib, was sentenced to death in person while standing in a cage wearing a prison uniform [c21]. Judge Fakhareddine al-Aryan announced Najib's sentence during a court session broadcast live on state television [c26]. Najib was sanctioned by the U.S. Department of the Treasury in April 2011 [c30] before being detained by Syrian security forces in early 2025 [c25]. The detention and alleged torture of teenagers accused of writing anti-government graffiti in Daraa in March 2011 had ignited the nationwide protests that escalated into civil war [c22]. The region has continued to see bloodshed, as about 1,500 mostly Alawite civilians were killed in retaliatory violence in March 2025, and over 1,700 people were killed in Suweida province in July 2025 [c28].

vocab.meaning: While not present at a trial or legal proceeding.
Done in response to an action, especially to seek revenge.

stories.headline: Russia frees former US Marine Robert Gilman after talks between Trump and Putin
stories.body:
Russia has released former U.S. Marine Robert Gilman from prison after more than four years following talks between U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin [c31]. Trump confirmed that Russia released Gilman on a humanitarian basis without demanding a prisoner exchange [c32]. Gilman, 32, was scheduled to land at Andrews Air Force Base in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday night [c34], and U.S. officials stated he would then be flown to a rehabilitation centre in San Antonio, Texas, for medical treatment [c38].

Gilman served in the U.S. Marine Corps from August 2019 until August 2020 [c37]. He was arrested in January 2022 on a train to Moscow for allegedly kicking a police officer while drunk, receiving an initial sentence of three and a half years that was extended to 10 years following alleged assaults on prison staff [c40]. However, his father, Vladimir Gilman, stated in an October 2024 op-ed that the police officer dropped charges and sustained no injuries [c39].

Advocate Eric Lebson stated that Gilman was transferred in June from a prison hospital to a psychiatric ward in a dissociative stupor due to prison abuse [c35]. U.S. Senator Ed Markey added that Gilman suffered from severe pneumonia and entered a near-death, catatonic state prior to his release [c36]. Meanwhile, Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the administration is seeking the return of Stephen Hubbard [c33], as Lebson noted five other Americans remain in Russian detention [c41].

vocab.meaning: Concerned with promoting human welfare and reducing suffering.
In a state of unresponsiveness or immobility.

stories.headline: András Baka elected Hungarian president as parliament enacts reforms
stories.body:
Hungary's parliament has elected former Supreme Court chief András Baka as head of state by a vote of 140 to 6 [c42]. All 51 attending lawmakers from Viktor Orbán's Fidesz party walked out of the parliamentary chamber in protest before the vote [c43]. Baka, who is scheduled to assume the presidency on August 19 [c50], previously served as a judge at the European Court of Human Rights for nearly 20 years before becoming president of Hungary's Supreme Court in 2009 [c47]. Orbán's government removed him from that post in December 2011, three years before his term expired [c48], but Baka later won an unfair dismissal case against Hungary at the European Court of Human Rights [c51]. Prime Minister Péter Magyar had initially offered the presidency to chess star Judit Polgár, who declined the role [c49].

The election comes as the government led by Prime Minister Magyar introduces major reforms, including constitutional amendments by the Tisza party that limit the prime minister to two terms in office and members of parliament to three terms [c45]. The government abolished the Sovereignty Protection Office and established the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office [c44]. In addition, public service radio and TV in Hungary have been off the air since July 9 while news programming undergoes restructuring [c46].

vocab.meaning: Formal changes or additions made to a law or constitution.
Organizing or altering a system or process in a new way.

stories.headline: US Navy helicopter fires missiles at cargo ship breaking Iran blockade
stories.body:
A U.S. Navy MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles into the engine room of the Panama-flagged M/V Vela Nova in the Gulf of Oman to disable its steering gear [c52]. The M/V Vela Nova is the third ship forcibly halted by U.S. forces since Washington reinstated its ports blockade on July 14 [c58]. During an earlier blockade between April 13 and June 18, U.S. forces disabled nine vessels and redirected more than 140 ships attempting to reach Iranian ports [c59].

U.S. Central Command stated that as of August 11, it had redirected 55 commercial vessels attempting to run the Iranian blockade, disabled three non-compliant vessels, and boarded two [c53]. To carry out enforcement operations, the U.S. Navy has deployed more than 15 warships in the Arabian Sea, including two aircraft carriers and an amphibious assault ship [c60].

Tensions in the region remain high. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, stated that the Strait of Hormuz "will not be opened until the United States changes its behaviour and accepts Iran’s conditions" [c56]. Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran on Tuesday for mediation talks with Iranian officials [c57]. Meanwhile, Yemen's government reported that Houthi strikes on a cargo ship carrying Saudi military equipment in the Red Sea killed six people and injured 10 [c54].

vocab.meaning: An act of sealing off a place to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving.
Intervention in a dispute to help bring about an agreement.

stories.headline: Pilot of turbulence-hit Air India flight tests positive for marijuana after 300-foot drop
stories.body:
The pilot-in-command of an Air India flight that suffered a sudden drop in altitude has tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory drug test, an official confirmed [c63, c66]. The drug test returned positive for the banned substance following an investigation into the flight's dangerous drop [c63]. Under regulations set by India's aviation regulator, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), a pilot who tests positive for psychoactive substances for the first time must undergo de-addiction treatment [c70]. If a pilot tests positive a second time, DGCA regulations mandate a three-year licence suspension, and a third positive result leads to the permanent cancellation of the pilot's licence [c70].

The safety incident occurred on August 4 aboard Air India flight AI2379, which was traveling from Phuket to Delhi [c62]. While operating in cruise, the aircraft experienced a sudden loss of altitude and dropped around 300 feet [c62]. The sudden drop resulted in injuries to 20 passengers and four crew members [c62]. Following the flight's arrival, 17 people were hospitalised due to the injuries sustained during the sudden drop [c69].

Preliminary findings have provided details about what occurred in the cockpit before and during the altitude loss. A preliminary defect report noted that the aircraft's autopilot disconnected [c67]. The disconnect triggered a stall warning and a flight control Electronic Centralised Aircraft Monitor (ECAM) message prior to the loss of altitude [c67]. During the actual loss of altitude on the Air India flight, the stall warning flashed in the cockpit [c61]. In response, the first officer executed a stall-recovery response to regain control of the aircraft [c61].

The investigation into the incident involves international aviation authorities. France's Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety (BEA) and technical representatives from Airbus are currently assisting India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau [c68]. The positive drug test results prompted immediate corporate and regulatory discussions. Air India's outgoing chief executive officer, Campbell Wilson, met with officials from the Civil Aviation Ministry and the DGCA on Tuesday evening following the test results [c64]. In a separate leadership change for the airline, former Ethiopian Airlines chief executive Tewolde Gebremariam was appointed as Air India's new chief executive officer and managing director [c65].

vocab.meaning: Affecting the mind, mood, or mental processes.
Medical treatment to help a person stop using addictive substances.

stories.headline: India examines security impact of new Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey defence pact
stories.body:
India is examining the national security and regional stability implications of a new defence agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey, according to External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal [c71]. The pact, known as the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, was signed in Mecca on August 7 by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif [c72].

A central provision of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement states that an armed attack against any one of the three signatory nations will be regarded as an attack against all three [c73]. This trilateral pact builds upon a previous mutual defence agreement that was concluded between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in September [c74].

In addition to addressing the new pact, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called on the international community to hold Pakistan accountable following recent unrest [c75]. His comments came after protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir caused more than 90 deaths [c75].

vocab.meaning: A party or nation that has signed an official agreement.
Involving three parties, groups, or countries.
